title: Game-breaking lack of enforcement against input broadcasting / multi-input automation

posts.name: The Dexter
posts.cooked:
To the EVE Online Support Team and Community Management,

I am writing this out of sheer frustration and anger regarding the current state of the game. Over the last six months, input broadcasting and multi-input automation have completely spun out of control, and CCP’s total lack of enforcement is actively destroying the game.

PvP has become a joke. My group roams looking for fights, only for a single player with 10 accounts to drop on us with every single ship warping, locking, and firing at the exact same millisecond. Go to Taisy right now, and you will see a specific players running missions with multiple Barghests that all warp and align simultaneously. This isn’t high-level multiboxing; it is blatant, automated input broadcasting.

What makes this completely ridiculous is that your support team does absolutely nothing. These players are reported dozens of times. Your Terms of Service explicitly state that input multiplexing is forbidden, yet there are zero consequences. When confronted, these botters and input-broadcasters literally tell us “good luck with the report,” because they know CCP will not touch them.

It is incredibly disheartening to watch a game I love be ruined by this behavior. By refusing to punish these cheaters, you are killing the sandbox. It feels like corporate greed has overtaken game integrity, allowing rule-breakers to run rampant just because they pay for multiple subscriptions.

EVE used to be an incredible experience back in the days. Today, playing against automated multi-input fleets from players who operate with total impunity has turned the game into a joke.

posts.name: Lataviane Vemane
posts.cooked:
I’ve been playing EVE long enough to understand that some multiboxing is at least nowadays part of the game. A “few” accounts, some coordination, and you can accomplish things solo that normally require a small group. That’s part of EVE’s sandbox, but personaly I’m no fan of multiboxing at all.

But what we’re seeing now is something entirely different.

The sheer scale of multiboxing today—entire fleets run by a single person, dozens of accounts synchronized, industrial operations that dwarf what normal players can achieve—has reached a point where it actively harms the broader player base. It’s not just “someone using a few alts.” It’s industrialized gameplay that pushes out smaller groups, trivializes risk, and distorts the economy.

This isn’t healthy for the game.

When one person can field the equivalent of a corporation’s worth of ships, it undermines the core of EVE: cooperation, conflict, and meaningful choices. It also creates a barrier for new players who simply cannot compete with someone running 20+ accounts in perfect sync.

And all of this is happening while CCP is increasing monetization and advertising at a pace that feels disconnected from the actual state of the game. More paid features, more “special offers,” more pressure to subscribe multiple accounts—while core gameplay issues remain unresolved.

EVE thrives when players feel their actions matter. When the universe feels fair, dangerous, and alive. Right now, it feels like the game is drifting toward “pay for more accounts, or get left behind.”

I’m not asking for multiboxing to be removed. I’m asking for limits, balance, and a recognition that extreme multiboxing is not the same as normal gameplay. And I’m asking CCP to focus on the health of the sandbox instead of pushing monetization that encourages the very behavior that’s damaging it.

EVE deserves better.
Its players deserve better.
And the long-term future of the game depends on addressing this.
